topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Transformer Architecture Anatomy
sections.content: Briefly define the two core components of a Transformer block: Attention (focusing on relationships between words) vs. MLP (the internal knowledge repository). Establish the metaphor: Attention is the 'search engine', MLP is the 'database'.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The capital of France is...', Attention finds the link between 'France' and 'capital'; the MLP provides the specific label 'Paris'.

sections.title: The MLP as a Key-Value Memory Bank
sections.content: Explain that an MLP layer consists of two linear projections with a non-linear activation (ReLU/GELU) in between. Conceptually, the first layer 'identifies' a pattern (Key), and the second layer 'writes' a specific output associated with that pattern (Value).
sections.example: Visualizing a 'memory slot': A neuron pattern representing the concept 'Mars' (Key) triggers a signal to the output layer that adds 'Red' and 'Planet' (Values) to the hidden representation.

sections.title: Mathematical Mapping: The Superposition Concept
sections.content: Explain the math via 'Weight Matrices'. The network acts as a distributed system where facts are stored as vector directions. Use a visual graph showing two weight vectors merging into a resultant 'fact vector' that updates the token's state.
sections.example: Graph visualization: A blue arrow representing 'Scientific Entity' and a red arrow representing 'Cold' converge in the vector space to pinpoint the location of 'Pluto' inside the model's weights.

sections.title: Case Study: Fact Updating (Editing the Database)
sections.content: Demonstrate what happens during inference. When the input 'The capital of...' passes through the MLP, the specific weights effectively act as a retrieval mechanism, adding a learned vector to the token embedding.
sections.example: Animation: Input 'Dog' enters the MLP -> The 'Domestic Animal' weight filter activates -> The model outputs the added feature 'Barks' into the token stream.

sections.title: Synthesis & Limitations
sections.content: Summarize that MLP stores facts in a 'diffuse' way (not in a single cell, but in patterns). Note the trade-off: this allows for generalization but makes precise fact-checking difficult.
sections.example: A library analogy: Attention is looking at the book titles; MLP is the content written inside the books. If the pages are torn, the model 'hallucinates' the facts because the weight patterns are fuzzy.
